node.title: Re: Strip specific html sequence
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Please see [id://1201438] for why it is indeed not a good idea to do this without a proper parser, especially look at the "spoiler" for lots of cases of perfectly valid HTML that will not be fun to parse with a regex. Here's an example with [mod://Mojo::DOM]:

use warnings; use strict; use Mojo::DOM; my $html = <<'ENDHTML'; Title
ENDHTML my $dom = Mojo::DOM->new($html); $dom->find('div > div.blue') ->each(sub{ $_->parent->remove }); print $dom; __END__ Title

I had a quick look at "[https://git-scm.com/download|Git for Windows]", and it happens to include [mod://HTML::Parser]. In the above thread, [tangent] showed an example with that module [id://1201544|here], and because it's a fairly old but good module you will find lots of examples with it online as well. That Git distribution also appears to contain [mod://cpan] as well, so you could try installing [mod://Mojo::DOM].
